summary.text: 听 has two documented uses: it is the standardized simplified form of 聽, meaning “hear” or “listen,” and an older graph for “smiling appearance.” These uses are distinct; the evidence does not show that one meaning developed from the other.

formation.text: For the older word meaning “smiling appearance,” the received analysis treats 听 as phonosemantic: 口 contributes a mouth-related meaning category, while 斤 is assigned a sound role. This analysis describes the older use, not how 听 came to represent 聽.

components.text: In the received analysis of the older smiling-word use, 口 supplies a mouth-related meaning category. This role belongs to that use of 听.

The received analysis assigns 斤 the sound role in the older smiling-word graph. A Zhengzhang transcription reports readings for both graphs, but the cited evidence does not establish a matched component–host comparison.

sound_limitation.text: The reported Zhengzhang readings for 听 and 斤 do not establish a sound match between this component and the older smiling-word use. The supplied Baxter–Sagart readings cover 聽 and 斤, but do not supply a reading for the older 听 word; current Mandarin readings likewise cannot establish the ancient relationship.

sound.text: A Zhengzhang transcription gives readings for 斤 and 听, but the evidence does not match either 斤 reading to a specific reading of the older smiling-word 听.
A Zhengzhang transcription also gives an alternate reading for each graph; the evidence does not establish their correspondence.
In modern Mandarin, 斤 is jīn and 听 is tīng. This current reading pair does not establish an ancient sound relationship for the older smiling-word use.

history.text: 听 has a received Shuowen entry for the older “smiling appearance” use, analyzed as 口 with 斤 as phonetic. The curated image is separately identified as a modern redraw of 聽 in Shuowen seal-script style; it does not depict the older 听 graph or establish a sequence of graphic changes.

A secondary proposal traces a vernacular form 𠯸, with 厅 as its sound element, to 听 through copying that assimilated 厅 to 斤. The intermediate form and this proposed graphic path have not been verified from primary manuscript evidence.

听 is the standardized simplified counterpart of 聽. It is also attested for 聽 in Song–Yuan vernacular writing; that graphic use does not show that the older smiling-word meaning developed into “hear” or “listen.”

uncertainties.text: The Han- and Tang-period literary examples attest the smiling sense but do not establish its first occurrence. The date and textual path by which 听 began representing 聽 are unresolved.

The proposed 𠯸-to-听 pathway and its 厅 sound element lack independent confirmation from primary manuscript evidence. The reported historical readings do not establish a matched comparison between 斤 and the older smiling-word 听.

senses.period: Han-period example cited; exact first attestation unresolved
senses.text: A cited Han-period literary example uses 听 for a smiling appearance. It attests this use by that period but does not establish when the word or graph first arose.

senses.period: Song–Yuan vernacular use attested; beginning date unresolved
senses.text: By the Song–Yuan period, 听 was used to write the separate word 聽, meaning “hear” or “listen.” The reason for this reuse is unresolved; the proposed 𠯸/厅 account has not been verified from primary manuscript evidence.

limitations.text: The smiling and hearing/listening uses are separately documented. No semantic development from “smiling appearance” to “hear” or “listen” is supported.

overview.text: 听 is the simplified form of 聽, meaning “hear” or “listen.” It also has a separate older use meaning “smiling appearance”; the two uses are not connected by a documented change in meaning.

items.period: Shuowen small-seal-script tradition; modern digital redraw
items.tradition: Small seal script, labeled 小篆 / 說文‧口部 by the character-specific Xiaoxuetang record
items.caption: This modern redraw shows the small-seal form recorded for 听 in the Shuowen 口 section. The received Shuowen entry gives 听 the sense “smiling appearance” and analyzes it as 口 with 斤 as phonetic.
items.alt: Black small-seal-style glyph on white: compact upright and cross strokes at left, beside a broader curved form on the right.
items.selection_reason: It depicts the 听 form associated with the older “smiling appearance” entry. The image does not illustrate 听’s separate later use for 聽.
items.rights: CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication; Commons also describes it as a public-domain picture of an ancient script. The linked Xiaoxuetang query-interface glyph imagery is separately covered by its CC0 notice.

limitations.text: This modern redraw is not an excavated artifact and does not establish the form’s archaeological date or a sequence of graphic changes. 听’s use for 聽 is separately attested by the Song–Yuan period; its beginning and the path between these uses remain uncertain.
